attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice and endorsed by him.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps both qualifiers: the hedge 'as far as I can tell' and the brand-recognition exemption. It also uses the post's own definition of a moat. The claim describes Marcus's own assessment rather than stating a flat fact.

contract.note: The contract rightly keeps the epistemic hedge and does not turn it into a firm claim that OpenAI had no competitive advantage apart from its brand. The statement gives no measurable standard for what counts as a moat, so any score would depend on a standard the evaluator supplied.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged report of Marcus's own judgement ('as far as I can tell', 'doesn't really'), and it sets no measurable standard for a moat. Market evidence could challenge the substance, but it could not settle what Marcus was able to identify unless the hedge were replaced with a firmer claim. The evidence packet is empty. The case is not broken; the claim is simply not adjudicable.
